verified_key_information_units.information: AS Tallinna Vesi reported strong financial performance in 2025 with revenue increasing 11.4% to €72.48 million, operating profit rising 11.8% to €21.22 million, and net profit growing 7.2% to €14.24 million. The company invested €55.74 million in fixed assets.
verified_key_information_units.source_evidence: Main financial indicators table; Statement of comprehensive income

candidate_sentences.text: The group reported total sales of seventy-two point four eight million euros, representing an 11.4 percent increase compared to sixty-five point zero eight million euros in 2024.
Operating profit increased by 11.8 percent to twenty-one point two two million euros compared to eighteen point nine eight million euros in the previous year.

Profit before taxes rose by 18.0 percent to seventeen point four three million euros, and net profit increased by 7.2 percent to fourteen point two four million euros, up from thirteen point two eight million euros.

Capital investments in fixed assets expanded significantly, reaching fifty-five point seven four million euros compared to forty-nine point five three million euros in 2024, focusing on infrastructure renewal, smart water meter installation, and environmental protection.

verified_key_information_units.information: Customer revenue mix shifted significantly due to regulatory tariff harmonization: private customer sales increased 18.3% to €31.84 million from higher consumption, while business customer sales decreased 2.7% to €16.76 million following reduced tariff rates for businesses.
verified_key_information_units.source_evidence: Sales section breakdown tables and text

candidate_sentences.text: Water services sales rose by 6.9 percent to sixty-two point three one million euros, largely supported by an 18.3 percent increase in sales to private customers within the main service area, which reached thirty-one point eight four million euros.
Conversely, sales to business customers decreased by 2.7 percent to sixteen point seven six million euros due to statutory price harmonization measures.

verified_key_information_units.information: Cost optimization and energy transition efforts reduced electricity expenses through the new combined heat and power plant at Paljassaare wastewater treatment plant, which supplied 43.8% of site electricity needs and increased renewable energy consumption to 87% of total energy use (from 23% in 2020).
verified_key_information_units.source_evidence: Energy use and energy consumption overview section

candidate_sentences.text: However, direct production costs remained stable at nine point nine zero million euros, as a 6.9 percent decrease in electricity expenses to four point three seven million euros offset higher chemical costs.

The reduction in electricity expenses was primarily achieved through the successful commissioning and operation of the combined heat and power plant at the Paljassaare Wastewater Treatment Plant, which generated all required heat and over half of the electricity needed for treatment processes.

verified_key_information_units.information: Infrastructure modernization advanced with smart water meter rollout covering over 80% of customers (targeting 100% by end-2026), construction of 45.1 km of pipes (49% via trenchless methods), and launch of trenchless sewer rehabilitation service by subsidiary Watercom renewing approximately 6 km of pipes.
verified_key_information_units.source_evidence: Investing for the Future; Watercom activities

verified_key_information_units.information: The company achieved 99.5% compliance with drinking water quality standards and was awarded 'Green Company of the Year'. Environmental initiatives included constructing 7.1 km of separate stormwater systems to reduce flooding and setting ambitious climate targets to reduce Scope 1 and 2 GHG emissions by 50% from 2020 levels by 2030 and achieve carbon neutrality by 2040.
verified_key_information_units.source_evidence: Highlights from 2025; Sustainability Statement; Climate change section

verified_key_information_units.information: The group maintained a strong liquidity position with €11.29 million cash balance at year-end and €160 million outstanding loans carrying an average interest rate of 3.24%. In December 2025, €5 million was drawn under a €25 million loan agreement with the Nordic Investment Bank to support future investments.
verified_key_information_units.source_evidence: Statement of financial position; Investors section

candidate_sentences.text: Total borrowings increased to one hundred sixty million euros following additional loan drawdowns, bringing the debt-to-assets ratio to 66.02 percent.

verified_key_information_units.information: Tallinna Vesi continued its dividend policy of distributing 50-80% of annual profit, paying €0.53 per share (80% of 2024 net profit) to shareholders in June 2025, balancing returns with investment needs.

Key 2026 strategic priorities include completing the smart meter rollout, harmonizing water tariffs for residential and commercial customers by summer 2026, advancing the ozonation project at Ülemiste water treatment plant, reconstructing secondary clarifiers at Paljassaare wastewater treatment plant, and executing planned investments of up to €60 million.

details.completeness_justification: K1, K2, K3, and K6 are PRESENT with clear evidence in the candidate summary. K4 (infrastructure modernization details), K5 (environmental compliance and awards), K7 (dividend policy), and K8 (2026 strategic priorities) are MISSING - no mention of smart meter rollout progress, stormwater systems, drinking water quality compliance, 'Green Company' award, climate targets, dividend payout, or 2026 strategic priorities. The summary covers most financial metrics and some operational highlights but omits several HIGH-importance strategic and environmental items, resulting in a Neutral/Mixed coverage assessment.
details.coherence_justification: The candidate summary is fully coherent internally. All statements are logically connected and support the overall narrative of financial performance improvement. There are no self-contradictions: growth metrics consistently show increases across revenue, profit, and investments. Explanations for changes (e.g., electricity cost reduction due to new plant, tax rate impact on net profit) are clear and logically connected to the surrounding statements. The organization flows logically from revenue breakdown to profitability metrics, cost analysis, and capital investments. There is no unnecessary repetition that would reduce clarity. All numerical relationships are presented as standalone comparisons without implying exhaustive additive relationships where they might not apply.
